reference.source: Sherlock's Diseases of the Liver and Biliary System / Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics
clinicalPearls: A developmental disorder of the biliary tree arising from malformation of the embryonic ductal plate, producing dense periportal fibrosis with abnormally shaped bile ductules
It is most often part of the fibrocystic disease spectrum and is strongly associated with autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease and mutations in PKHD1
The characteristic presentation is portal hypertension with splenomegaly and variceal bleeding, while hepatocellular synthetic function is typically well preserved
Portal hypertension here is presinusoidal, so liver enzymes and synthesis are often near normal despite significant complications
It frequently overlaps with Caroli disease and other ductal plate malformations, warranting assessment of the whole hepatobiliary and renal system
Recurrent cholangitis may occur when there is associated biliary ductal dilatation
Management targets complications, including variceal bleeding, cholangitis, and associated renal disease, with liver or combined liver-kidney transplantation in selected cases
reference.pathophysiology: During normal development the embryonic ductal plate remodels to form the intrahepatic bile ducts. In congenital hepatic fibrosis this remodelling is arrested, leaving a ductal plate malformation in which persistent, irregularly shaped and ectatic bile ductules are embedded in broad bands of dense portal fibrosis. This fibrosis expands the portal tracts and compresses the portal vein branches, producing presinusoidal portal hypertension while sparing the hepatocytes, so synthetic function is largely maintained. The same ciliopathy mechanism, frequently due to PKHD1 mutations affecting fibrocystin, links the liver lesion to renal cystic disease and to overlapping conditions such as Caroli disease.
additionalInvestigations: Abdominal ultrasound and cross-sectional imaging of liver and kidneys
Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography to define biliary anatomy and detect ductal dilatation
Liver biopsy showing the ductal plate malformation and portal fibrosis
Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy to screen for and grade varices
Renal function tests and imaging for associated polycystic kidney disease
Genetic testing including PKHD1 where indicated
redFlags: Haematemesis or melaena from variceal bleeding
Fever with jaundice and right upper quadrant pain indicating cholangitis
Progressive renal impairment from associated kidney disease
Rapidly enlarging spleen with worsening cytopenias from hypersplenism
reference.prognosis: Because hepatocellular function is usually preserved, the outlook depends chiefly on control of portal hypertensive complications, recurrent cholangitis, and the severity of associated renal disease; many patients do well for years, and transplantation is reserved for refractory complications.
pitfalls: Mistaking preserved liver enzymes for absence of significant disease despite marked portal hypertension
Overlooking the associated renal cystic disease that may dominate the long-term prognosis
Failing to distinguish presinusoidal portal hypertension from true cirrhosis
Not screening for and managing oesophageal varices before a first bleed
Missing coexisting Caroli disease and the associated cholangitis and stone risk
references: Sherlock's Diseases of the Liver and Biliary System
management: No drug reverses the fibrosis; management targets portal hypertensive complications, with endoscopic surveillance and band ligation of oesophageal varices
Use non-selective beta-blockers for primary and secondary prophylaxis of variceal bleeding

Treat acute variceal haemorrhage with resuscitation, vasoactive agents such as terlipressin or octreotide, endoscopic band ligation and antibiotic prophylaxis, reserving a portosystemic shunt (TIPS or surgical) for refractory bleeding
Treat recurrent cholangitis promptly with antibiotics where there is associated biliary ductal dilatation or Caroli disease, and consider prophylaxis for recurrent episodes
Assess and manage associated autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease with renal function monitoring and nephrology input
Reserve liver transplantation, or combined liver-kidney transplantation, for refractory portal hypertension, intractable cholangitis or end-stage renal disease
Offer genetic counselling and family screening for PKHD1-related fibrocystic disease and coordinate hepatology, nephrology and clinical genetics
